svg.title: Spin-native weights
svg.desc: Three parts. Left: a sphere carrying 120 icosian directions as dots, drawn schematically. A trained quaternion is an arrow; snapping it to the nearest icosian leaves a mean direction error of 14.75 degrees, and adding a second residual icosian at a quarter of the size pulls the result to within 4.73 degrees. Middle: the 120 by 120 product table as a grid; picking a weight icosian and an input icosian lights one cell that reads out the product icosian, followed by a shift and at most two adds. This part is described in the records but the kernel was never built. Bottom: held-out bits per byte, lower is better: dense width 256 1.4078, quaternion width 256 1.4959, dense width 152 with equal parameters 1.5136, icosian pair with a 2-bit mantissa 1.5148, with snapped activations 1.5343, dense width 128 1.5520, and a single trained icosian snap 1.6344. The equal-parameter pair 1.5136 and 1.5148 are level within noise.
svg.text: Spin-native weights: round to one of 120 rotations, correct once, read a table
1 Snap a quaternion to a rotation, then correct it
Mean direction error: 14.75° with one icosian,
4.73° with a residual pair (about 9 times less
error energy). Single snap: mean cosine 0.965.
Exact group table: all 14,400 products matched
A kernel that serves block products by table read was never
written, so no speed or energy has been measured.
3 Held-out bits per byte (lower is better)
At equal width the quaternion model
Sphere and dot layout are schematic; the angles in the zoom are drawn to the stated ratio. Numbers are from the records. Status: parked.
